newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares hit new high, fuelled by Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares hit new high, fuelled by Ericsson.

text.p: Sweden's sharemarket rose on Tuesday to a new all-time high, opening a touch firmer but a little nervously in line with the U.S. but then taking its lead from telecoms company LM Ericsson.
The Stockholm general index rose 1.04 percent to 2,470.00, a new all-time high close that beat Monday's record close.
Turnover was a relatively high 4.88 billion crowns with brokers reporting a lot of money around in the market.
"There is a lot of money in the market at the moment," one broker said.
The trading sector was the best performer, up 4.99 percent.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz was the day's winner, jumping 70 crowns to 1,135 amid rumours of a share split and ahead of a Q4 report. This followed a 55 crowns rise on Monday.
Telecoms major Ericsson rose 6.5 to 235.5 crowns, making most of its gains in late afternoon trade once New York opened.
"There's nothing really new that's happened," a broker said.
Astra slipped two to 331.5 crowns amid market rumours about a delay in FDA approval for an anti-asthma drug.
Car safety equipment maker Autoliv rose 10.5 to 320 crowns after U.S. partner Morton Internatiaonl was strongly traded.
